release_contents:
Phase 3 Steps 1-6 (the bilingual admin UI/UX sweep), 12 commits since the last deploy (edf1c12): 9f120b9, fd9b729, 58de025, cf58313, 9ed4706, aff623f, 575af47, b028548, a1d80dd, f42a55a, 5995a84, 47af559.

Step 1 — finished the PHP controller/model/service translation sweep started in an earlier session: all 21 admin controllers with Bengali UI text now route it through __()/status_options()/option_options() (ActivityController, ObjectiveController, RoleController, PositionController, CommitteeMemberController, UserController, CommitteeController, OrganizationUnitController were the last 8), a full re-survey of app/Models and app/Services found only intentional STATUSES/TYPES constants remaining plus two real gaps: three Notice/JobPosting model methods shared with the public API (left untouched; the three ADMIN views calling them switched to option_label() instead) and three upload-validation services (PhotoUploadService/ApplicationDocumentService/NoticeFileService) whose Bangla-only RuntimeException messages are surfaced to admins — added upload_error_label(), an admin-only reverse-lookup, without touching the services themselves (still Bangla-only for the public API paths that also use them).

Step 2/3 — built the reusable [বাংলা][English] tabbed bilingual content editor (components/admin/bilingual-field.blade.php: Bootstrap nav-tabs, missing-translation + validation indicators per tab, no-data-loss-on-tab-switch, native keyboard nav, dark/light via existing theme tokens) and applied it to all 14 stacked bn/en input spots across 13 admin form views.

Step 4 — made recruitment/applications/document.blade.php (the printable/PDF application document, shared by print() and pdf()) bilingual via a new ?doclang=bn|en param defaulting to the admin's current panel locale; applicant-submitted text is never translated, only the document's own chrome (labels/headings/footer).

Step 5 — final bidirectional hardcoded-string scan: no stray Bangla found outside intentional branding/comments; found and fixed 5 stray English literals that bypassed __() entirely (Mission/Vision card title+badge, role System/Custom badges, membership Student badge, activity Featured badge, the Send-password-reset button).

Step 6 — regression coverage added throughout: StatusAndOptionHelpersTest (upload_error_label), BilingualEditorTest (18 tests — every bilingual form renders the tabs, missing-indicator, validation-tab-selection, no-data-loss), BilingualApplicationDocumentTest (7 tests — doclang default/override/fallback, applicant text verbatim in both languages), HardcodedStringScanTest (automated Bengali-literal scan) + HardcodedEnglishStringsFixedTest (6 tests), LocalePersistenceTest (10 tests — the switcher endpoint + SetAdminLocale's full user>session>cookie>default precedence chain, none of which had direct coverage before).

No new migrations, no new routes, no schema changes — purely admin-UI/lang-catalog/PHP-controller-body/Blade-view/test changes. Full local suite: 525 passed, 2193 assertions, before this deploy's own build re-ran it (also green).

post_deploy_production_e2e: DONE (HTTP-level) — this session has no browser-automation tool connected, so this E2E is a scripted, authenticated curl session against the live site rather than a real browser; every functional check that doesn't require an actual rendered viewport passed. Used a TEMPORARY QA account (created via a one-shot cron script, super_admin role, @provatferi.invalid email — the real Super Admin's password was never touched, per standing policy) for the whole pass, deleted at the end. Verified: (1) fresh guest GET /login renders bn by default (lang="bn", 'প্রশাসনিক লগইন'-era content). (2) Login succeeds; post-login /admin renders bn by default. (3) POST /locale locale=en persists — a completely fresh subsequent GET /admin (new request, same session) renders lang="en" and English brand text. (4) All 13 major modules (activities, notices, recruitment, committees, membership seasons/types, objectives, about, org units/positions, roles, users, recruitment-applications) return 200 under the English locale. (5) Real Bangla-only content data (e.g. ActivityType names with no _en yet) renders as-is under the English locale — confirmed NOT machine-translated, matching the fallback policy. (6) The [বাংলা][English] tabbed editor is live on production's real create/edit pages. (7) Created a throwaway, hidden (active=0) test Objective with real bn+en text, confirmed both values round-tripped on reload with no data loss. (8) Edited only the English side and re-saved; reload showed the English change applied AND the Bangla side byte-for-byte unchanged. (9) Switched the admin locale back to bn; the same record's Bangla text was still exactly as originally entered. (10) Triggered the same required-field validation error once under each locale: bn showed 'বিবরণ আবশ্যক।', en showed 'The Description field is required.' (11) Deleted the test record — confirmed 404 afterward, zero residue left in production content. (12) Fetched a REAL existing job application's printable document (read-only, no mutation) via ?doclang=bn and ?doclang=en: chrome text differed correctly ('স্বেচ্ছাসেবী আবেদনপত্র'/'আবেদন নম্বর' vs 'Volunteer Application'/'Application No.') while the applicant's own submitted name was byte-identical in both. (13) Downloaded the real PDF in both languages: both are genuine PDFs (%PDF- header), different byte sizes confirming distinct per-language content. (14) All 10 static assets (CSS/JS/icons/favicon) referenced by a real admin page returned 200 — no failed asset loads at the HTTP level. One real issue surfaced DURING testing, root-caused, and confirmed to be a test-authoring artifact rather than an application bug: an em-dash typed into a curl test payload was mangled by the local shell into an invalid Latin-1 byte before transmission; MySQL's utf8mb4 column correctly rejected it with a clean PDOException (atomic failure, no partial write, no security issue) — retrying with the same content minus that one mis-encoded character succeeded immediately. NOT verified this pass, and explicitly flagged rather than silently skipped: actual rendered light/dark theme appearance, actual responsive behavior at mobile/tablet breakpoints, and real browser console JS errors — all three need a real browser/visual tool, which was not connected in this session. All temporary artifacts (QA account, staged diagnostic scripts, their containing directory) were removed by the end of this pass; verified via a follow-up 404 on the script path and an empty cron-jobs list.

cron_timing_note: Cron runs in UTC. One-shot crons scheduled 5-8 minutes ahead on specific minutes, read once via the cron-jobs output operation, then deleted immediately — none left armed (verified empty via a cron-jobs list call after smoke-test-live). One migrate-check attempt in this deploy returned an empty output body on its first scheduled run despite the job existing and the scheduled time having passed; recreating the identical cron fresh (new uid) and waiting the same interval succeeded immediately with full JSON output — treat a genuinely empty (not malformed) cron output body as possibly transient and worth one clean retry with a new uid before assuming the underlying script failed silently.
release_manager_path_reminder: release-manager.php lives at the PRIVATE path /home/u951246149/domains/provatferi.org/laravel-admin-releases/_tooling/release-manager.php for every step after the one-time install — NOT under public_html/admin/. The upload step's own generateUploadURLV1 call must target the domain admin.provatferi.org (the subdomain itself), not the parent provatferi.org — the parent domain's upload URL roots at that domain's own public_html (wrong tree entirely for this subdomain's docroot), while the subdomain's own upload URL roots directly at its docroot, matching upload-release.mjs's un-prefixed `_release_staging/...` destination path exactly.
never_fetch_a_staged_script_url: Requesting a staged one-shot script's URL EXECUTES it (it is under the web-servable docroot). Verify removal with the file listing tool instead.
local_mariadb_note: Confirmed running (mysqld.exe) before this deploy's local build-release.sh run — no repeat of the earlier stalled-build incident this deploy.
curl_csrf_testing_note: When scripting a POST to a CSRF-protected route (e.g. /locale) with curl, fetch the CSRF token and set the cookie jar in the SAME request that will be reused for the POST, not across separate GET calls with the jar re-opened each time — doing it in two disjoint GET calls produced a spurious 419 in an earlier session even though the actual endpoint was working correctly.
